evidence.supports: for every n, n mod 2 = 0 or n mod 2 = 1

evidence.notes: Applies the theorem at `n = 7` and confirms its INFERRED type is exactly `Or (Eq (mod 7 2) 0) (Eq (mod 7 2) 1)`, with a negative control that it does not also state `Or (Eq (mod 7 2) 0) (Eq (mod 7 2) 2)` -- a control that differs in ONE literal, deliberately, since a control transposing whole subterms would make the kernel run a failing defeq with no early exit. Also asserts the two disjuncts are NOT def_eq to each other, so the split is not vacuous. `Nat.lt_two_cases` is checked in the same test at `r = 0` against a `zero_lt_succ 1` witness.
evidence.supports: the disjunction is the stated one, its two sides are different propositions, and lt_two_cases applies

formal.statement: theorem Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Or (Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.mod x0 (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))) AxNat.zero) (Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.mod x0 (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)))

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*).

This is the lemma `crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/nat_prelude/bitwise.rs`'s module doc named as absent -- "a `Nat.mod _ 2 in {0,1}` case-split lemma this prelude does not yet carry" -- and which two lanes independently sized as blocking work. The prelude's nearest pre-existing relatives were both strictly weaker: `powsq.rs`'s PRIVATE `mod_two_eq_one_of_ne_zero` produces only the `= 1` half and requires the caller to already hold `r != 0`, and `Nat.even_or_odd` states a `div`-shaped disjunction (`n = n/2 + n/2` or `n = succ (n/2 + n/2)`) that never mentions `Nat.mod` at all.

The eliminator form callers actually use is `ops::cases_mod_two`, which takes a motive that VARIES with the remainder's value; this theorem is the propositional statement of the same fact.
statement: Every natural number's remainder on division by two is either zero or one.
title: n mod 2 = 0 or n mod 2 = 1
